{{Short description|Japanese literary award}} {{Infobox award | name = Naoki Prize | subheader = 直木三十五賞 (Naoki Sanjūgo Shō) | image = | imagesize = | alt = | caption = | awarded_for = Best work of popular literature by rising author | presenter = [[Society for the Promotion of Japanese Literature]] | country = Japan | reward = | year = {{start date and age|1935}} | website = {{url|https://www.bunshun.co.jp/shinkoukai/award/naoki/}} }} The '''Naoki Prize''', officially {{nihongo|'''Naoki Sanjugo Prize'''|直木三十五賞|Naoki Sanjūgo Shō}}, is a [[Japanese literature|Japanese]] [[literary award]] presented biannually. It was created in 1935 by [[Kikuchi Kan]], then editor of the [[Bungeishunjū (magazine)|''Bungeishunjū'']] magazine, and named in memory of novelist [[Naoki Sanjugo]].{{cite journal|title=Accounting for Taste: The Creation of the Akutagawa and Naoki Prizes for Literature|last=Mack|first=Edward|journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies|date=2004|volume=64|number=2|pages=291–340|doi=10.2307/25066744|jstor=25066744}} Sponsored by the [[Society for the Promotion of Japanese Literature]], the award recognizes "the best work of popular [[literature]] in any format by a new, rising, or (reasonably young) established author."{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081121132314/http://www.jlit.net/reference/awards/awards_n_to_z.html|archive-date=November 21, 2008|url=http://www.jlit.net/reference/awards/awards_n_to_z.html#naoki_sanjugo|title=Literary Awards, N-Z|work=JLit|access-date=August 8, 2018}} The winner receives a watch and one million [[yen]].{{cite web|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2012/02/14/reference/literary-awards-run-spectrum/|title=Literary awards run spectrum|work=[[The Japan Times]]|last=Fukue|first=Natsuko|date=February 14, 2012|access-date=August 8, 2018}} Kikuchi founded the Naoki Prize with the [[Akutagawa Prize]], which targets a new or rising author of literary fiction. The two prizes are viewed as "two sides of the same coin" and inseparable from one another. Because of the prestige associated with the Naoki Prize and the considerable attention the winner receives from the media, it, along with the [[Akutagawa Prize]], is one of Japan's most sought after literary awards of recognition.{{cite encyclopedia|url=http://www.britannica.com/EBchecked/topic/11844/Akutagawa-Prize|title=Akutagawa Prize|encyclopedia=[[Encyclopædia Britannica]]|publisher= [[Encyclopædia Britannica Online]]|access-date=August 8, 2018}} ==Winners== [[Bungeishunjū]] maintains the official archive of past Naoki Prize winners.{{cite web|url=https://www.bunshun.co.jp/shinkoukai/award/naoki/list.html|language=ja|title=直木賞受賞者一覧|trans-title=Naoki Prize Winners List|publisher=[[Bungeishunjū]]|access-date=August 30, 2018}} ===1st–100th === {|class='wikitable' |- | rowspan=2|1935 |1 |[[Matsutarō Kawaguchi]] |{{nihongo|''Tsuruhachi Tsurujirō''|鶴八鶴次郎}},
